messages:
From: Tariq Hassan <tariq@acmecorp.com>

Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 08:13:22 -0800
Subject: High 504/429 rate impacting checkout (severity: p0)

Kimberly —

We're seeing a sudden surge of 504s and 429s from calls to /v1/generate since ~07:45 PT. Our checkout path relies on short, synchronous completions and user-facing latency is spiking (p95 ~27s). Our SRE stack shows a ~22% 5xx rate and 18% 429 rate across the past 20m. Retry storms are compounding the queue — the upstream client is retrying with exponential backoff but the backlog still grows.

We need an immediate mitigation plan (can you pause batching or pin to a lower-traffic model?) — this is blocking checkout for some customers. I've attached a short timeline and logs.

Attachments: acme_timeline_11-27.csv, diagnostic_dump_20261127.log

—Tariq
Head of Platform Ops, Acme Corp

On Fri, Nov 27, 2026 at 8:21 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Monica and Rishi are on call and looking at runtime traces now.

Quick summary from runtime:
- Symptoms: sudden increase in queue depth on the frontend worker pools serving Acme (~8x baseline), leading to CPU+mem pressure and stalled async batching threads.
- Error profile: majority are 504 gateway timeouts from the routing proxy; some 429s are emitted when the batching coordinator rejects oversized micro-batches.
- Suspected proximate cause: prefix KV-cache thrash causing excessive cache misses and long tail token decode times, which increases per-request service time and amplifies queueing.

Actions taken (08:12–08:25):
- Disabled cross-request prefix coalescing for Acme (hotpatch) — reduced p95 in a small canary by ~40%.
- Throttled concurrent inflight for the Acme routing key by 25% to stabilise backlog.
- Collected heap and KV hit-rate histograms; attaching logs.

Next: need product/eng decision on shipping a short-term config that disables aggressive prefix batching for customer tenants experiencing thrash, and a follow-on code fix to address eviction fanout in the KV layer.

—Monica
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 08:39:03 -08:00
Subject: Re: High 504/429 rate impacting checkout (severity: p0)

Folks —

Short update after digging into traces and the KVS metrics:
- The eviction fanout bug causes an edge-case where a single warmed prefix invalidation triggers synchronous repopulation across many worker shards. When inbound QPS rises, repopulation latencies multiply and cause request backpressure.
- In the wild this shows as long tail token-decode spikes (some decodes hitting 600–900ms extra), which cascades into 504s and 429s from the batching layer.

Proposed immediate mitigations (need quick sign-off):
1) Toggle: disable prefix repopulation on eviction (skip synchronous repopulation, keep cold fetch on demand). Expected stabilization in 10–15m.
2) Routing: divert new non-critical traffic to a spare pool (we can give Acme a temporary endpoint) — helps reduce effective QPS on the hot path.
3) Customer-facing: offer a credit and propose a short SLA exception while we fix root cause.

If leadership approves, I'll prepare the hotfix PR.

—Rishi
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Tariq —

We implemented a hotpatch at 08:32 PT (disabled repopulation + reduced concurrent inflight). Early telemetry shows 5xx rate fell from 22% to 5% in the canary; p95 dropped from ~27s to 9s. We're continuing to monitor.

Immediate asks for Acme:
- Please route ~30% of non-critical traffic to the secondary endpoint we provided (sidecar-2) for the next 24 hours while we stabilize.
- We'll share a timeline for the permanent fix by EOD PST.

We're also preparing a credit/SLA exception; Lauren, can you draft the exception and commercial note? Monica/Rishi will produce a technical postmortem.
